{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — RadialSpark Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side) 
**Re:** Playbook review of the Contractor MSA — verified findings and redline positions

---

## 1. Executive summary

We reviewed the Agreement against 19 playbook rules. Nine clauses are compliant, eight are deviations requiring redline, and two rules are unaddressed by the document.

The commercial architecture is favourable to us in the places that usually cost the most. Ownership of deliverables under § 4 sits at or above our fallback: the "Works" vest in Company, Contractor's retained rights are confined to its own pre-existing tools and know-how, and we take a perpetual, royalty-free, sublicensable licence to any embedded Contractor Information. There is no exclusivity, no minimum commitment, no MFN, no non-compete, no audit right against us, no liquidated damages or exit fee, and no auto-renewal window we can miss (the term is evergreen with a mutual 15-day exit when no Statement of Work is outstanding).

The gaps cluster in risk allocation and exit. The Agreement contains **no operative indemnity at all** — the § 7 heading refers to indemnification but the clause carries only caps and waivers — which is walk-away territory under our playbook. Liability is capped at fees paid under the relevant Statement of Work rather than 12 months' fees, and the sole carve-out cross-refers to the Independent Contractor clause, so it is a dangling reference with no indemnity, confidentiality, gross negligence or wilful misconduct exception. There is no conformance warranty or remedy (with implied warranties disclaimed), no transition assistance or data return on exit, no Customer right to terminate for convenience once an SOW is under way in an indefinite term, and no cyber cover despite Contractor handling our Confidential Information and accessing our systems. Governing law is Arizona with mandatory arbitration, both outside our accepted list. Finally, the § 4(c) licence and § 10 assignment clause do not survive an M&A event or extend to affiliates.

Our redlines target the fallback in every case except termination for convenience and transition assistance, where the fallback has no sensible application to an evergreen, task-by-task engagement.

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 4 (Ownership of Materials Related to Services; Acceptance) | At or above fallback; Works vest in Company, no Vendor licence in our data. Licence not expressly "irrevocable" — noted only. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 4 (Ownership of Materials) | § 4(c) runs to Company alone; no affiliate coverage and § 10 blocks transfer to a successor. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 6 (Termination) | Convenience right available only when no SOW is outstanding, in an indefinite term. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 1 (Purpose of Engagement) | Task-by-task engagement; no sole-supplier or requirements obligation. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties | Compliant | § 6 (Termination) | No exit fee, kill fee or late-payment penalty; termination pays only fees earned. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 4 (Ownership of Materials) | No field-of-use or non-compete restriction on our business. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 7 (Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor) | Arizona law plus mandatory arbitration under § 19; both outside accepted positions. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 5 (Representations and Warranties and Warranty Disclaimer) | No conformance warranty, period or remedy; § 5(e) disclaims implied warranties. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 6 (Termination) | No transition assistance, data export or deletion obligation anywhere. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Deviation | § 7 (Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor) | Mutual and solicitation-only, but term-plus-one-year and no advertising/unsolicited carve-outs. |
| Medium | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 7 (Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor) | § 10 requires consent even for a successor in a merger or asset sale. No Vendor change-of-control termination right. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 3 (Contractor's Compensation) | No audit or inspection right binds Company; satisfied by absence. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations | Compliant | § 3 (Contractor's Compensation) | No MFN, benchmarking or right-to-match obligation on Company. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant | § 3 (Contractor's Compensation) | Time-and-materials per SOW; no minimum, retainer or take-or-pay. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 1 (Purpose of Engagement) | Evergreen term with mutual 15-day exit; no auto-renewal mechanic to qualify. |
| Low | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | § 7 (Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor) | **No operative indemnity anywhere**; heading is misleading. Walk-away item — see § 3. |
| Low | LOL-CAP — Liability cap, mutuality, carve-outs | Deviation | § 7 (Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor) | Cap is fees paid under the relevant SOW; sole carve-out cross-refers to § 9 (Independent Contractor). |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Deviation | § 7 (Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor) | CGL and E&O at USD 1,000,000 each, but no cyber/privacy cover. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

1. **Absence of any Vendor IP indemnity (§ 7).** The Agreement contains no indemnify / hold harmless / defend language at all. The § 5(c) non-infringement warranty does not fund the defence or damages of a third-party IP claim. Our playbook treats the total absence of a Vendor IP indemnity as walk-away territory. We have inserted our fallback as a new § 7(d): a Contractor third-party IP indemnity with the customary Company-modification, combination and specification exclusions; procure / modify / replace remedies with a refund of fees paid where no option is commercially available; and a 3x annual fees super-cap expressed to override the § 7(a) cap so the indemnity is not swallowed by it. This is not a drafting preference and we should not sign without it.

No other finding reaches walk-away territory. In particular, the assignment clause carries no Vendor termination or re-pricing right on our change of control, and the non-solicit is mutual and solicitation-only (no no-hire), so both are ordinary fallback negotiations.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Send the redline with § 7(d) (IP indemnity) and § 7(a) (cap) as linked, non-negotiable items.** The cap fix — mutual, fees paid in the 12 months preceding the claim, with Excluded Claims for indemnification, confidentiality breach, gross negligence and wilful misconduct — is what makes the new indemnity meaningful. Flag to Contractor that the existing carve-out cites § 9 (Independent Contractor) and is plainly a drafting error.
2. **Press the exit package as a single block:** a Company right to terminate the Agreement or any SOW for convenience on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees (and a bar on Contractor convenience termination while an SOW is outstanding, so the existing mutual 15-day gap-period right survives untouched); plus the new transition paragraph in § 6 — six months' assistance at then-current rates, data return in a machine-readable format within 30 days, certified deletion thereafter. Note internally that the T4C redline was machine-repaired and should be read once more before issue.
3. **Governing law and venue:** move to New York with exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County, preserving temporary injunctive relief elsewhere, and rename the retained § 19 heading so no arbitration reference dangles. Delaware, California or England and Wales are acceptable alternatives if Contractor resists New York.
4. **Short-form asks, low expected friction:** add the fallback warranty package to § 5 (90 days software conformance to documentation, 30 days Services, repair / replace or refund); add cyber and privacy liability cover of USD 2,000,000 to the existing clause 14 sentence; add a mutual successor-assignment carve-out on written notice to § 10; extend the § 4(c) licence to Company's affiliates on written notice and make it transferable to an M&A successor; and re-anchor the § 13 non-solicit to 12 months after the individual's involvement ends with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs.
5. **Do not reopen** the compliant clauses. § 4 ownership, the absence of exclusivity, minimums, MFN, non-compete and audit rights, and the evergreen term with no renewal window all favour us; we should protect them rather than invite reciprocal drafting.
6. **For the business:** § 3(b) allows Contractor to change rates on 30 days' notice with no cap. That is a pricing point outside the rules reviewed here, and we flag it for commercial input rather than legal redline."}
